state.webSettings.queueIntro: Agents ({name}, maintainers, sub-agents) search the web and read pages in the order below: the top one comes first, and if it fails (error, timeout, no results, low balance) the next one takes over. Reorder or turn them off, but keep at least one. Shared across all devices; changes apply from the next call. DeepSeek and Ergo's built-in browser search share the same tools, web_search and web_fetch, told apart by engine: an agent that sets engine uses only that method (enabled ones only); without engine the queue decides, and each result's title line says which one was actually used.
state.webSettings.toolsHint: agent-browser means the agent drives Chrome itself from bash: when it's first, agents search and download with it first. Turning it off only stops it being used for search; downloading files and operating pages still work. The built-in browser in the HarmonyOS app is only used by {name}, in turns where you talk to it from the browsing sidebar or floating button (skipped otherwise): when it's ahead in the queue, {name} first opens the search results in the browser on your phone and reads and clicks there. Turning it off only stops it being used for search; {name} can still click, fill in fields and upload files on pages when you ask. Tavily isn't in the queue and can only be requested once its key is configured.
